questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a closure in JavaScript?

options.text: A function that has access to its outer lexical scope even after the outer function has closed.
A method to forcibly terminate an infinite loop.
A built-in data type used for storing encrypted keys.
A private variable declared with the private keyword.

questions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding state (the lexical environment).

questions.stem: What does an async function in JavaScript always return?
questions.explanation: Async functions always return a promise. If the return value is not explicitly a promise, it is automatically wrapped in a resolved promise.

questions.stem: In the JavaScript Event Loop, which queue is checked and processed before the Macrotask (Callback) queue?

options.text: The Microtask queue (e.g., Promise callbacks, queueMicrotask)
The file I/O thread pool queue

questions.explanation: All microtasks in the microtask queue must be completely executed and drained before the event loop proceeds to the next macrotask.
